title: Cost predictability vs. quality: a rapid ops & platform micro-deck
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Cost predictability vs. precision: how platform/SRE teams trade off unit economics and response fidelity
Speaker note: one-liner for execs + a quick technical hook for SEs.

Slide 2 — Why this matters (context for platform engineers)
- Large customers report unpredictable token spend during peak periods — procurement pain + surprise invoices
- Platform teams want SLOs for cost per request + latency + correctness (tension: saving $$ can harm hallucination/formatting)
- Typical ask: 'Give me a safe knob to reduce spend by 30% without raising customer complaints'

Slide 3 — The trade space (visual: 2D axis, cost vs. output precision)
- Cost levers: batching, KV-prefix caching, model quantization, routing to smaller variants, reserved pools
- Precision levers: full fp model, larger context windows, ensemble rescoring, reranking
- Key insight: not all requests need same precision — categorize by payload & downstream tolerance

Slide 4 — Customer segmentation for action (ops-friendly categories)
- Tier A (end-user facing, high-precision): low batch, fresh model, dedicated capacity if SLA-critical
- Tier B (internal analytics, tolerant): aggressive quantization + batched endpoints + cached prompts
- Tier C (background jobs): async, low SLO, extreme batching + cheap model variants

Slide 5 — Redwood levers mapped to customer tiers (product mapping)
- Hosted API: quick experiments (A/B quantize on dev traffic), streaming to measure latency impact
- Dedicated: reserve smallest pool sized for Tier A; move Tier B to lower-cost nodes via routing policies
- Private: policy + KMS + audit-friendly controls for municipalities/regulated industries (calls out auditability when enabling quantization)

Slide 6 — Practical playbook for SE + seller (step-by-step)
1) Run quick eval set (30–100 prompts) with customer's golden references — measure baseline cost & accuracy (metric suggestions below)
2) Apply low-risk optimizations: prefix cache + small-batch guardrail -> measure delta
3) Try quantization on Tier B traffic only (canary 1% -> 10% -> 50%)
4) If accuracy drop > threshold -> fallback policy to higher-precision model per request type
Notes: show sample thresholds and scripts in appendix.

Slide 7 — Metrics to show in POC / pilot dashboards (what matters to buyer)
- Cost/1000 tokens by route (USD) (before/after)
- P95 latency by route
- Regression rate on golden prompts (fraction of prompts below quality threshold)
- Failure / fallback rate (how often we hit fallback to full-precision model)
- Estimated savings projection over 90 days (simple linear extrapolation)

Slide 8 — Seller talking points & objections (short bullets)
- Objection: 'If we quantize, answers get worse' -> Response: "We can route high-risk prompts to unquantized model and run canary evals with your dataset."
- Objection: 'We need predictable billing' -> Response: "Reserved Dedicated pools + per-route quotas + spend alerts reduce surprises; we can commit to consumption bands for pilots."
- Sweet spot messaging: "Balance is programmable — you choose precision per route, we enforce it."

Slide 9 — Mini demo script for SEs (6–8 minutes)
- Start with a dashboard snapshot: baseline cost + error on golden set
- Enable prefix cache -> show immediate cost delta (live demo/simulated)
- Toggle quantization on route B -> show regression metric + fallback hits live
- Show routing policy that routes by header tag (x-priority: high/low) -> show split in logs

Slide 10 — Sample canary checklist (operational)
- Create golden prompt set (30-100)
- Define pass/fail thresholds (regression % <= 2% or consumer impact metric)
- Canary schedule: 1% traffic for 24h -> 10% for 48h -> 100% 
- Set automated rollback: > threshold -> instant revert
- Notify: ops + acct exec on each step (slack channel template included below)

Slide 11 — Sales appendix: short technical appendix for SEs (quick snippets)
- Example routing policy (pseudocode):
  route(request) { if (request.meta.priority == 'high') -> model:xx_fp32; else if (len(request.prompt) < 512) -> model:yy_q4; }
- Cost calc example: 
  baseline: 0.12 USD per 1k token; q4 variant: 0.035 USD per 1k token -> projected 70% token cost reduction on routed traffic
- Log sample for fallback events (fields sellers look for): request_id, route, model, fallback_reason, latency_ms

Slide 12 — Open questions / to validate with customers (notes to self)
- How tolerant are customers to brief format differences vs. semantic regressions? need examples per vertical (e.g., legal vs. commerce)
- SLA billing guarantees: what discounts/commitments can legal sign off on? (loop in finance)
- Do we need a special contract term for quantization/auditing? (ask security/compliance)

Slide 13 — Next steps (internal)
- Draft two short demo videos: (1) cache + batching (2) quantization + fallback (owner: Jamal)
- Build a pilot template sheet for sales to capture golden prompts + pass thresholds (owner: Priya)
- Align with product on a per-route quota UI mock for console (link to PRD: INF-PRD-allocations-v0.2)

Slide 14 — Appendix: Checklist for legal/compliance asks
- Preserve logs of fallbacks for 90 days
- Provide customers with regression report for each pilot phase
- KMS/HSM notes: quantized models are still processed — include data residency checks for private deployments

Slide 15 — Raw notes / fragments (scratchpad)
- TODO: gather 3 real customer prompt sets from CS (non-identifiable) to include as examples
- Idea: interactive 'what-if' calc in seller playbook (input: requests/day, avg tokens, current spend -> outputs predicted savings) -> product wants this
- Slack thread where we started design: #go-to-market-cost-plays (Jamal pinned messages)

--- END ---

Draft tone: intentionally concise, split between quick seller-openers and SRE/engineer-level playbook. Keep this as a companion to a one-pager and a 6-slide public-facing deck.

Unresolved: need to sync with product-hosted-api on estimated quantization impact by model family (open action: tag Priya).
